document.title: Instructions for Form PENS.E/2-C — Payment Instructions for a Residual Settlement and Any Retroactive Benefit Due

chunks.heading: Purpose of form PENS.E/2-C
chunks.text: Upon the death of a participant or retiree, a residual settlement and/or any retroactive benefits due but unpaid at death may be payable as a one-time payment to the person(s) or institution designated by the participant/retiree on form PENS.A/2. Form PENS.E/2-C requests payment of this residual settlement and/or retroactive due but unpaid benefit.

chunks.heading: When a residual settlement becomes payable
chunks.text: A residual settlement becomes payable if: the participant died in service with no eligible survivors under articles 34/35bis/35ter/36/37; the participant died after service but before electing a benefit, with 5+ years of contributory service and no eligible survivors; the participant died during entitlement to a retirement-type or disability benefit and (i) no further benefits are payable to survivors and (ii) total benefits paid were less than the participant's own contributions plus interest; or the participant had survivors entitled to benefits and, after all survivor entitlements end, the total amount paid by the Fund is still less than the participant's own contributions plus interest.

chunks.heading: What counts as a retroactive due but unpaid benefit
chunks.text: A retroactive due but unpaid benefit arises if, at the time of death, a benefit (retirement, early retirement, deferred retirement, disability benefit, or withdrawal settlement) was payable but had not yet been disbursed, including payments returned by the participant's bank but properly payable.

chunks.heading: Who receives the residual settlement/retroactive benefit
chunks.text: It is payable to the beneficiary(ies) designated by the participant on form PENS.A/2. If more than one recipient was designated, they share equally unless the participant indicated otherwise on PENS.A/2. A designated recipient must be alive when payment is due; a predeceased recipient's share is distributed among surviving recipients in proportion to their own shares.

chunks.heading: Payment for a recipient under 16
chunks.text: Each recipient must submit their own payment instructions. If the recipient is a child under age 16, payment is made to the custodial parent or legal guardian; if there is no custodial parent, UNJSPF requires the appointment of a legal guardian to act on behalf of the minor child.

chunks.heading: What happens if there is no PENS.A/2 on file
chunks.text: If there is no duly completed, dated and signed form PENS.A/2 in the Fund's records, any residual settlement and/or retroactive due but unpaid benefit will be paid to the deceased's estate instead.

chunks.heading: Section 2: designated recipient information
chunks.text: Provide the recipient's full name exactly as shown on a passport or official government ID, date of birth, sex, and contact information. If the recipient is an institution, provide the institution's name, identification/registration number, and contact information.

chunks.heading: Section 3: currency of payment for a residual settlement
chunks.text: Default currency is USD, but a one-time payment may be paid in the currency of the recipient's choice; if a currency other than USD is selected, the bank converts the payment without UNJSPF's involvement.

chunks.heading: Documents to enclose with form PENS.E/2-C
chunks.text: A valid government-issued photo ID (for institutions, the ID of the representative), and a recently dated bank statement/document (e.g. voided cheque) matching the payment instructions and the Fund's records.

chunks.heading: Signature authentication requirement for PENS.E/2-C
chunks.text: The recipient's signature must be authenticated in the presence of a UN official, government official, or notary public, who completes their printed name, email, official title/licence/index number, signature, authentication date, and official stamp/seal.
